title: THE GATEKEEPER SHE FINISHED THE SENTENCES OF
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE FLOCK THAT FILED A FLIGHT PLAN
candidates.premise: Four hundred thousand starlings have begun to fold themselves into black walls across the approach path of Karst Lowfield airport every dusk, and in six weeks two aircraft have gone around with minutes of fuel to spare. Air traffic controller Femi Adeyinka has noticed that the shapes repeat like sentences. The authority has approved a cull and a laser line for Friday, and Femi has asked for one night to be proved wrong.

candidates.title: THE GUARDIAN WHO WAS ONLY A STORY
candidates.premise: For three hundred years travellers crossing the Vael Pass in winter have told of the Lantern Woman, who shows a light in the whiteout and leads the lost to the hut. Dr. Samira Habib's survey has just proved that no such person ever existed and that the lights are a cluster of lamps lit by herders and their descendants. The village that keeps the lamps has stopped lighting them out of embarrassment. In the first blizzard of the season the Lantern Woman, who is made of the retelling itself, begins to thin, and the pass begins to kill.

candidates.title: THE SLOW WARD
candidates.premise: In the Tessel Valley an old fold in time makes one hour outside last three weeks inside. Dr. Isaure Brandt has run a hospital there for eleven years and keeps forty-one patients alive with extra clock-time that no other ward can give. Their families outside have counted nine thousand days each waiting at the gate, and the valley is closing: the fold is tightening and will seal in six outside days. Dr. Brandt will not discharge anyone she cannot finish treating. The families will not wait any longer.

candidates.title: THE STRIKE OF THE SMALL GODS
candidates.premise: The doors of Marrowgate have started to stick, the crossroads to flood with confused traffic, the kettle to refuse the second whistle. The city's small gods (of doorsteps, of crossroads, of the third stair, of the last bus) have walked off the job, because nobody has said thank you in four generations and the one old shrine that the council is about to close was their only mailing address. Illuminara is asked to find a fair settlement before the winter traffic and the old people's heating, both of which depend on small things working, fail.

candidates.title: THE LAST VETO OF THE QUIET REACH
candidates.premise: The Concord of the Thousand Suns acts only by unanimity. For four hundred years the Last Speaker of the Quiet Reach, a dying people of three thousand, has voted No to every proposal and the Concord has learned to stop asking. Now a drifting dark pair of black holes is bending a route that carries four billion lives through the Reach, and the one measure that will work needs her signature. Illuminara is asked to find a way round the veto. She decides first to ask the Speaker what she is saying No to.

candidates.title: THE QUARANTINE THAT HAD A DOOR
candidates.premise: A federation of universes has sealed Home Universe 12 behind a quarantine because its physical constants are slowly leaking across the membrane and damaging three neighbours. The Examiner assigned to certify the seal, Veyra of the Fourfold Court, has a duty and a conscience; the people of the quarantined world do not know they are sealed. In six days the Examiner must either confirm the permanent closure or recommend an unsealing that her court says will cost three worlds. Illuminara is asked to stand for the sealed world.

candidates.title: THE WALL THAT PAINTED BACK
candidates.premise: On Sorrel Street a forty-metre mural made by three generations of neighbours has begun, overnight, to repaint itself: first a swallow, then a crane, then a line of bulldozers eating the block. The council has approved a clinic and the owners will demolish the wall in nine days. The mural, which has become a mind of paint and communal grief, answers any approach with new images. Dr. Ines Marchetti, who fought for the clinic for nine years, is losing sleep and patience.

candidates.title: THE INVENTOR WHO WOULD NOT BE RESCUED
candidates.premise: Bisi Okonjo has built a cheap, local water filter that can save a delta of forty thousand people from a cholera season, and she has refused every offer of help from Illuminara and every large organisation, because the last time a patron took up her work they put their own name on it and her village was erased from the credit and the licence. The filter is three weeks from its first real test and has a failure Bisi cannot find. Illuminara knows she could find it in an afternoon. Bisi has asked her not to.

candidates.title: THE GATEKEEPER SHE FINISHED THE SENTENCES OF
candidates.premise: The tide-gate of Ostmark has been worked by feel for fifty years by Halvard Beck, 79, and a surge that will overtop the delta town of nine thousand is thirty hours away. Illuminara reads the failing mechanism in minutes, corrects Halvard's account before he finishes it, and is right every time. By evening he has locked the gate-house and gone silent, and the one thing the gate depends on is the thing he cannot yet say. His granddaughter Runa, the engineer who wants the gate automated, is the only person he will still talk to.

candidates.title: THE TWO WHO STILL HAD THE WORD FOR RAIN
candidates.premise: Only two people alive speak Ilumet, the language of the Saltmarsh villages, and they have not spoken to each other since 1989. Adaora Tennant and Pel Orsolo are both eighty-one. A schoolteacher, Dani, has a grant, a recorder and four months to record and teach what they know. When one of them dies the language dies with her, and neither will enter the other's house. Illuminara is asked to help, and she decides she cannot translate between them: she can only sit with them and find out what stands between two people who share a word for rain.

selection.title: THE GATEKEEPER SHE FINISHED THE SENTENCES OF
selection.reason: First available story in the original editorial order; no reader ranking is claimed.
selection.risk: The premise could make Illuminara's first mistake feel contrived, turn Halvard's silence into a lesson-delivery device, or resolve the emergency through an apology followed by unearned trust. The flood must not be treated as a convenient punishment for her impatience, and Runa must remain an engineer with her own judgment rather than a translator between two principals.

rounds.summary: This is the corrected set's clearest new dramatic engine: Illuminara's formidable speed becomes the obstacle without making her weak, while Halvard's tacit craft, Runa's engineering judgment and the approaching surge create a concrete test that dialogue alone cannot satisfy. The love-direction is embodied in restraint, patient listening and preserved authorship, and the local scale gives the day an immediate human opening.

R14 check before prose. Aim: the tide-gate holds against the surge, nine thousand people stay dry, and the one man who knows the gate is not made redundant by being rescued. Counterpart: Halvard Beck (79; wants to be asked, not to be right; his tacit craft has never been written down because nobody waited for the end of his sentences), Runa Beck (engineer; drew the array so he would never climb the ladder in a storm, and heard her own love read as a headstone), Idun Maas (chair; legitimate duty to nine thousand, will not hang the town on one visitor or one old man). Strongest objection on the page: Maas in scene 2 and again in scene 5 (two-for-two is not a law; she will remember tonight as the night they were lucky), and Runa's refusal to pretend the array can learn the seat in a day. What Illuminara must understand: her speed is the obstacle; the missing variable is not only a fact (a tongue of silt under the left seat) but a timing (the water leans the foot down and packs it) that her force sense, which reads what pushes and not when, would not have reached. Love in action: she says plainly what she did, sits on the step all night with no correction, asks one question per hour or so, holds the sentence she already has (the coin in her mouth), and then carries only the cracked bearing and touches nothing else. Freely chosen change: Halvard opens the bolt at 04:30, makes two time-bound predictions, authorises the writing and signs Maas's order; Maas keeps her own fallback (the dike, a 22:10 deadline); Runa turns the left wheel on his word. A vivid, unusually disciplined draft. Illuminara's over-fast understanding creates a real mistake without making her incompetent; Halvard's two predictions are written before measurement, Runa supplies independent instrumentation and Maas retains authority. The held sentence is love expressed as costly restraint, and the gate, compensation, shared manual and conditional trust make the result concrete. Three causal improvements remain: Halvard's deepest objection is inferred rather than spoken, Maas's fallback does not yet visibly protect all nine thousand people if the gate stays open, and the ending still leaves the future system dependent on 'the man who hears it' without proving Runa can inherit the signal.

Revision of T01 answering GPT's T02 review (REVISE_BEFORE_FINAL). Everything the critic asked to protect is kept: the three right readings and the wrong one, the plain admission, the coin held in the mouth, Halvard's answer going one step beyond hers, the two signed predictions tested against rod and tuner, Maas's signature requirement and refusal of permanent dependence, the day-one cost and the conditional trust. Changes are local: one spoken objection in scene 3, a life-safe fallback and its cost in scene 5 with its echo in scene 6, and a first verified transfer of knowledge in scenes 6 and 7. Power decides nothing between beings; Illuminara's one physical act remains carrying the diagnosed bearing. Outcome: gate holds, nine thousand safe, Fisher's Row compensated, Halvard credited and no longer the sole interpreter, with trust returning as a rule.

T03 fully answers the three causal requests without losing the draft's restraint. Halvard now states the wound in his own cadence and Illuminara answers by not explaining him to himself; Maas's abort branch protects every life at a real, named cost; Runa proves one bounded transfer of craft and the manual makes succession testable. The gate still holds because evidence, consent, Halvard's knowledge, Runa's engineering and Illuminara's limited physical help work together. One local numerical contradiction should be corrected before final: Halvard says she was right four times while the deck and Illuminara's admission establish three right readings and one damaging mistake.

Final. GPT's T04 review found T03 ready for final after one local continuity correction, and that is the only prose change: Halvard's line in The Step now reads 'Three times you were right, and the one time you weren't it sounded the same', matching the deck, Illuminara's own admission and the scene-one sequence (three right readings, one damaging wrong one). Everything the critic asked to protect is untouched: his spoken objection and its two-line cadence, her withheld answer and the coin in the mouth, the life-safe Salt Meadow fallback, Runa's independent call, the three-note certification rule, the bounded bearing and the conditional rule at breakfast. Outcome unchanged: gate holds, nine thousand safe, Fisher's Row compensated, the method credited to both Becks and now teachable, trust returning as a rule.

final_critic_line: Illuminara repairs the harm of finishing Halvard's sentences by learning to wait for the knowledge her force-sense cannot supply; Halvard, Runa and Maas each retain authority, the gate holds under a measured and life-safe plan, and the craft becomes teachable without erasing its first keeper.
